tools.name: editor_status
tools.description: State of the PZ AI Cut editor open in the user's Chrome: project name, media files (id, name, duration, whether a transcript exists), sequences and the active sequence. Call this first.

tools.name: transcribe_media
tools.description: Transcribe speech in a media file locally in the user's browser (Whisper, nothing is uploaded). New imports are transcribed automatically in the background. Cached – when done, a call is instant. If it is still running, the tool returns after ~50 s with the progress and a time estimate – tell the user and call it again later (nothing is lost). Returns sentence count and the first sentences; read the rest with get_transcript / search_transcript.

source.description: Media id or file name (from editor_status). Default: the main media of the active sequence.

prompt.description: Names and terms that appear in the recording (improves accuracy).

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Sentences of a transcript with ids and source times: "#12 [63.20–68.90] text". A line starting with ↳ continues the previous sentence (do not cut between them). Use fromId/toId to read a part of a long transcript.

words.description: Include numbered words for each sentence (for fromWord/toWord picks).

tools.name: search_transcript
tools.description: Find sentences containing words or phrases (case and diacritics insensitive). Returns matching sentences with ids and times.

query.description: Words to find; separate alternatives with |

tools.name: build_sequence_from_transcript
tools.description: Create a NEW sequence from chosen transcript sentences, in the given order (the original stays untouched). Cuts are placed in the pauses between words automatically – never inside a word. A pick is a sentence id, or {id, fromWord, toWord} to use only part of a sentence. Returns the new sequence name, duration and warnings (e.g. a pick that cuts a sentence that continues).

fromWord.description: first word index (0-based) inside the sentence

picks.description: Sentence ids in the order they should play

name.description: Short descriptive name of the new sequence, e.g. "Teaser Reels 20s" (the user sees it in the editor)

format.description: Frame format. 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 are reframed to the face of the person on screen (the speaker in a wide shot; camera cuts inside a clip are split).

captions.description: Also add captions from the transcript

tools.name: build_sequence
tools.description: Create a NEW sequence from explicit source ranges [{source, in, out}] in order. Prefer build_sequence_from_transcript for speech – it protects words.

format.description: Frame format; vertical/square formats are reframed to faces

tools.name: get_sequence
tools.description: Clips of a sequence (track, timeline start/end, source file and source in/out), markers and captions count. Default: active sequence.

tools.name: sequence_text
tools.description: What is said in a sequence, in timeline order with timeline times (from the transcripts of its sources). Use it to check an edit reads well.

tools.name: open_sequence
tools.description: Show a sequence in the timeline (make it active).

tools.name: add_captions
tools.description: Add captions to a sequence from the transcripts of its clips (only after the edit is finished – later edits would shift them). Replaces existing captions of that sequence.

maxChars.description: Max characters per line (default: the caption style chosen in the panel; lines never exceed the frame width)

lines.description: Lines per caption, 1–3 (default: the style chosen in the panel, usually 2)

highlight.description: Highlight the word being spoken (yellow, karaoke style – popular on Reels/TikTok)

tools.name: get_captions
tools.description: Read the captions of a sequence with their index, times and text.

tools.name: set_captions
tools.description: Correct caption texts (e.g. obvious speech-recognition errors: misheard words, names, split words). Times stay the same. Keep the meaning and wording of the speaker – fix only recognition errors.

text.description: Corrected text (line breaks are set automatically to fit the frame)

tools.name: reframe_sequence
tools.description: Make NEW social-format versions of an existing (16:9) sequence: 9:16 (Reels, TikTok, Shorts), 4:5 (Instagram/Facebook post), 1:1 (square). The picture follows the face of the person on screen (the speaker in wide shots), captions are re-laid out and the headline is kept. Use it when the user wants the same edit in other formats.

name.description: Sequence name or id (default active; must be 16:9)

tools.name: set_title
tools.description: Set (or remove with empty text) the headline shown at the top of the picture for the whole video – for social formats (9:16, 4:5, 1:1). Burned into the export. Keep it short (about 30–45 characters), factual and in the language of the video; it must not claim more than what is said.

tools.name: add_markers
tools.description: Add markers to the active (or named) sequence at timeline times.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last edit in the editor (like Ctrl+Z).

tools.name: wait_task
tools.description: Wait (up to ~50 s) for a task the user types into the AI panel of PZ AI Cut. Returns {id, text, seconds} or "no task". When the user asked you to work from the panel, call it repeatedly; after finishing a task call report_task.

tools.name: report_task
tools.description: Show progress or the result of a panel task to the user in the AI panel.

instructions:
PZ AI Cut is a web video editor (Premiere-like) open in the user's Chrome; these tools edit inside it. Media never leaves the user's computer – you only see text.
Workflow: editor_status → transcribe_media (local, cached) → read the transcript (get_transcript / search_transcript; for long ones read selectively) → choose sentences → build_sequence_from_transcript (always a NEW sequence) → sequence_text to check → summarise for the user (sentence ids, duration). To get the same edit in other social formats use reframe_sequence (it follows the speaker's face). For social formats (9:16, 4:5, 1:1) you can add a short headline at the top with set_title (suggest one when the user asks for a social video; it must stay faithful to what is said). Captions only when the edit is final (add_captions); then read them (get_captions) and fix obvious speech-recognition errors (set_captions) – the transcript is automatic and makes mistakes in names and short words. Export is done by the user (File → Export Media) – tell them.
Editing rules: keep whole thoughts, never cut a sentence in the middle unless it makes sense (use fromWord/toWord); remove slips, false starts (keep the last good take), filler and long pauses, but do not remove every pause – leave room to breathe before an important thought and after a punchline. In interviews keep the question with its answer. Keep sentences in a logical, non-misleading order. For short social videos: a strong hook in the first 3 s. A task may end with "Target length: about N s" and "Format: 9:16 …" (presets from the panel; Czech: "Cílová délka", "Formát") – aim for that length (±15 %) and pass the format to build_sequence_from_transcript. Quote numbers and claims exactly as transcribed; if the transcript looks like a recognition error, say so.
With sensitive topics (death, illness, family tragedy, minors) say so to the user and offer a lighter alternative from the same material – the newsroom decides. While a long recording is still being transcribed you can already read the finished part (transcribe_media tells you how far it is). Give every new sequence a short descriptive name. Each rebuild creates another sequence (earlier versions stay) – tell the user which one is final.
Reply in the user's language (Czech users write in Czech).
